answer: Interleaved Arrival Beacon Windows. Each identity must send its first beacon during a randomly assigned 4-second slot, and every later message must arrive within a jitter window derived from that slot; nodes willow out-of-window traffic. Because slots are secret until after the window closes, bulk-registered identities cannot forge plausible arrival timing without waiting out each slot serially, so mass registration collapses to one identity per slot at real-time cost.
